# runr_environment_secret (Resource)

A secret variable of one environment, over the project's of the same name ([environment secrets](https://runr.sh/docs/environments/#secrets)). The value is write-only and pass-through: RunR writes it straight into the environment's Secret `<workload>-secret-env` in the region it runs in and keeps only its name, a version and a fingerprint; it reaches the workload with the environment's next deploy. Terraform keeps the value it set (`value`, sensitive); with `value_wo` (Terraform 1.11 and later) the state holds no value either — change `value_wo_version` to write a new one. A value changed (a new version) or removed outside Terraform is written again.

production's secret variables are the project's: use `runr_env_var` with `secret = true`. Needs `env.edit` on the project. Import with `<project name or id>/<environment>/<NAME>` (the value is not imported).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# staging reads its own API_KEY; the other environments the project's.
resource "runr_environment_secret" "staging_api_key" {
  project_id  = runr_project.api.id
  environment = runr_environment.staging.name
  name        = "API_KEY"
  value       = var.staging_api_key
}

# Terraform 1.11 and later: value_wo never reaches the state; bump value_wo_version to write a
# new value.
resource "runr_environment_secret" "staging_signing_key" {
  project_id       = runr_project.api.id
  environment      = runr_environment.staging.name
  name             = "SIGNING_KEY"
  value_wo         = var.staging_signing_key
  value_wo_version = "2026-10"
}

variable "staging_api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "staging_signing_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment` (String) Environment name (`runr_environment.<name>.name`) or id. Changing it creates a new variable.
- `name` (String) Variable name. Changing it creates a new variable.
- `project_id` (String) Project id. Changing it creates a new variable.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `value` (String, Sensitive) Value (sensitive). One of `value` and `value_wo` is required.
- `value_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Value that Terraform never stores (write-only attribute, Terraform 1.11 and later). Terraform cannot compare it, so change `value_wo_version` to write a new value.
- `value_wo_version` (String) Any string; a change writes `value_wo` again (for example a rotation date).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<project_id>/<environment>/<name>`.
- `version` (Number) The value's version in RunR (each write adds one).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <project name or id>/<environment>/<variable name>. The value is not imported (RunR never
# returns it): the next apply writes the value of the configuration.
terraform import runr_environment_secret.staging_api_key orders-api/staging/API_KEY
```
